author: Sevoo
body:
Hi guys.I was recently thinking about how unfair it is for donors to get increased exp.I think it really defeats the purpose of the game.But,most people like that idea,so I thought of a compromis.

Players can customize the amount of exp they want for kills and objectives!

But donors can always maximise the amounts of exp they want.

The command that I'm thinking of is

/amount xp kill/objective (amount)

So for instance,of people want a challenge for prestige,they do

/amount xp kill 0.5 or 1

Hope you Guys enjoy my idea!

- Sevo

replies.author: FrozenThorn
replies.body:
Donors get more XP because they have donated; it is there as a perk so that Donors do not feel like they have donated for no reason. In addition to this, Donors getting more XP and other perks is a way of persuading non-donors to donate so that they can get the same perks as the Donors; this then means Avicus gets money so that it can continue to function. 

If us non-donors could customise the amount of XP we got then most of them would maximise the XP amount so that they get more out of playing; others may not, therefore some of the non-donors will get more XP than others, making the game unfair.

replies.author: MasterProX
replies.body:
Looks like you completely missed Sevo's replies... he said that the customized XP amount would still cap at its current normal value; you can lower the amount of XP you receive per kill, for instance, but not raise it.

The only possible use for this I can conceive — besides transient content for taking a more challenging route — would be to set your per-kill XP value to zero so you can save your final kill before getting prestige for a select person (in other words, temporarily halting your XP gain until your best friend comes online so you can kill him and prestige without having to wait), which is still a shallow reason. Moreover, unless it would indicate somewhere on your profile, you couldn't really prove that you got all your XP at a handicapped rate, so this (superficially unnoticeable) feature would appeal only to personal satisfaction...

I just don't think that effectively implementing this feature would be worth all the trouble.
